Each of the 11 entries carries a query_rule which Postgres materializes as a SQL view over L2.<br>• L2 is the harvested record - one row per ARC. Shared core (GeoJSON Feature + properties) is identical across domains; domain-specific fields live inside the assays[] sub-resources.<br>• L3 is not a separate document - it is a promotion contract. Selected L2 fields become CQL2 queryables (and OAI-PMH facets). Promotion is governed by an explicit rule (right column).<br>• A single ARC can satisfy several membership rules → it appears in multiple collections simultaneously (cross-membership is intrinsic).<br>• Controlled-vocabulary registry (vocabularies.yaml) is the single source of truth for enum value spaces referenced by both L2 schemas and the L3 queryable list." vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="125" width="1380" x="76" y="810" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

div.div:
• L1 is hand-curated and lives in YAML. Each of the 11 entries carries a query_rule which Postgres materializes as a SQL view over L2.
• L2 is the harvested record - one row per ARC. Shared core (GeoJSON Feature + properties) is identical across domains; domain-specific fields live inside the assays[] sub-resources.
• L3 is not a separate document - it is a promotion contract. Selected L2 fields become CQL2 queryables (and OAI-PMH facets). Promotion is governed by an explicit rule (right column).
• A single ARC can satisfy several membership rules → it appears in multiple collections simultaneously (cross-membership is intrinsic).
• Controlled-vocabulary registry (vocabularies.yaml) is the single source of truth for enum value spaces referenced by both L2 schemas and the L3 queryable list.
